newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Berisha says rebels "obstacle" to poll.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Berisha says rebels "obstacle" to poll.

text.p: President Sali Berisha said on Wednesday that so-called rebel committees controlling much of southern Albania were an obstacle to a general election due by the end of June and must be disbanded.

Berisha told international mediator Franz Vranitzky that the committees had been created by the Socialist Party, which was in opposition until joining a unity government with his own Democratic Party last month. Vranitzky said the elections were "in a way imperilled" by the situation.
"The committees are a Socialist Party creation," Berisha told Vranitzky, an envoy of the Organisation of Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE). Reporters attended the talks.
Berisha said the crux of the problem was an agreement at the end of March between the government and the rebels. He said he considered the government had given them its support.
Rebels seized control of the south in an insurrection sparked by the collapse of dubious savings schemes earlier this year. They have demanded Berisha's resignation.

Asked by Vranitzky if the problem could be resolved, Berisha said: "Yes...They (the Socialist Party) could ask them to dissolve the committees...We are waiting." Vranitzky told reporters that much work remained to unblock the situation.
